A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniAVGen, with matching authors, core methods, and main experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends after the references; v2 additionally includes Supplementary Material, Sections 6–11, which was inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons in Table 1, interaction and modulation ablations in Tables 2–3, and qualitative and training-strategy results in Figures 4–7.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a user study, conditional-generation benchmark results, and further ablations in supplementary Tables 4–9.

M1.justification: The dual-branch architecture, asymmetric aligners, FAM, MA-CFG formulation, five task interfaces, and three-stage training remain unchanged. The supplement documents alignment, placement, and inference choices for the existing framework; it does not establish that the underlying method changed from v1.

E1.justification: Supplement Section 9 adds public-benchmark evaluation on GRID for video-to-audio dubbing with unseen-speaker reference audio and EMTD for audio-driven half-body animation. These conditional tasks already appeared in v1's training framework, but their benchmark evaluation coverage is new. The original training datasets and 100-sample joint-generation test remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds StyleDubber and EmoDubber as evaluated dubbing comparators. Table 9 also explicitly compares MA-CFG against vanilla CFG and no CFG. The main Table 1 comparator set remains unchanged; the EMTD comparison and user study reuse existing baseline models.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 34-participant preference study assessing audio quality, video quality, and audiovisual coherence. New conditional evaluations use GRID Dubbing Setting 3.0 and EMTD, introducing LSE-D, FID, and FVD measurements alongside retained metrics. These are additional evaluation protocols; the original test composition, training budgets, and main evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Supplement Tables 7–8 newly test which layers receive interaction modules and where modules enter each DiT block. Table 9 quantitatively compares four guidance policies, including restricted-interval MA-CFG, extending v1's qualitative guidance analysis. The original interaction, FAM, and training-strategy ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging three independent Gemini evaluations per sample. The supplement repeats this practice without introducing new seed counts, repeated-training information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. The 34-participant count describes the new study's sample size rather than an uncertainty-reporting change.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results, apart from equivalent decimal formatting. New Table 4 reports UniAVGen preference shares of 68.90%, 62.60%, and 74.30% for AQ, VQ, and AVC. Table 5 reports GRID LSE-C/LSE-D/WER of 7.59/6.11/10.64, leading both dubbing comparators. EMTD results are mixed: UniAVGen has the best reported FID but worse FVD than both comparators. Tables 7–9 add placement and guidance results, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The flow-matching losses, attention and interpolation equations, mask formulation, and guidance equations retain their mathematical substance. Changes to parameter-index notation are equivalent. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the supplementary implementation explanations do not introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly frames the abstract around human-centric generation and promotes the already-reported benefit of staged multi-task training into the abstract and introduction. The conclusion drops the explicit claim that FAM adds no significant computational overhead. The principal architectural contributions and overall performance claims remain.

C2.justification: The supplement adds explanations for interleaved and before-self-attention module placement, and identifies an alignment-versus-image-quality tradeoff for unrestricted MA-CFG. It explains restricted guidance as a mitigation. Section 11 newly states concrete limitations: absent video-aligned ambient-sound generation and constrained multi-person audio generation associated with the text encoder.

D1.justification: Sections 6–7 supply previously unavailable details: A2V window size 1/2, handling of one-frame versus four-frame video latents, 50-step Euler sampling, Vocos decoding, guidance scales 3 and 2, interval [0.5, 1], empty-text unconditional sampling, and the full Gemini scoring prompt. Section 10 additionally documents interaction insertion choices. These substantially expand reproducibility information without demonstrating changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for dubbing methods, benchmarks, inference components, and related generators, including VoiceCraft-Dub, MOVA, AudioX, and CMMD. However, the three-paradigm related-work organization and substantive positioning against UniVerse-1 and Ovi remain largely unchanged; this is an extension rather than a reframing.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. v2 revises the abstract, moves the introduction's task-unification discussion, clarifies the V2A motivation, shortens the conclusion, and adds acknowledgements. The new supplement has dedicated implementation, evaluation, ablation, and limitations sections, but the existing paper is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from a compact three-task schematic to a full-width opening display with generated examples for four modes. Existing figures and tables are substantially resized, and Figure 5 is relocated. The supplement adds six tables, Tables 4–9, displaying new evidence rather than merely renumbering existing results.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves support for the claimed task unification through GRID and EMTD evaluations and adds human preference evidence. The new placement and guidance ablations expose design choices and an important quality tradeoff, while implementation details and the evaluator prompt address major documentation gaps in the supplied v1. Explicit limitations also clarify applicability. Study-protocol detail and uncertainty reporting remain limited, but the added evidence and reproducibility information provide a substantial net improvement without relying on unchanged headline scores.
